related_questions.question: Can you see muscle-invasive bladder cancer on a CT scan?
related_questions.snippet: CT urography with and without contrast is the most appropriate initial imaging test for MIBC. CT can detect the primary tumor and most other tumors except for extremely small tumors.

related_questions.question: What is the gold standard for muscle-invasive bladder cancer?
related_questions.snippet: Radical cystectomy (RC) has historically been accepted as the gold standard treatment for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), supported by a large body of long-term evidence.

related_questions.question: What is a CT simulation for bladder cancer?
related_questions.snippet: This planning session, called simulation, usually includes getting imaging tests such as CT or MRI scans. This helps the doctor map where the tumor is in your body. You'll be asked to empty your bladder before simulation and before each treatment. Most often, radiation treatments are given 5 days a week for many weeks.
related_questions.title: Radiation Therapy for Bladder Cancer | American Cancer Society

related_questions.question: What is the difference between muscle-invasive bladder cancer and bladder cancer?
related_questions.snippet: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer is a serious and more advanced stage of bladder cancer. MIBC is when the cancer has grown far into the wall of the bladder (Stages T2 and beyond). For patients with MIBC, the overall prognosis (how the disease may progress) is based on stage and treatment.
